verses.text: When Jesus had finished praying, he went out with his followers and crossed the Kidron Valley. On the other side there was a garden, and he and his followers went into it.
Judas, who was betraying him, knew the place too, because Jesus had often met there with his followers.
So Judas came to the garden, leading a group of soldiers and some guards sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees. They were carrying lanterns, torches and weapons.
Jesus knew everything that was going to happen to him. So he went out and asked them, "Who are you looking for?"
"Jesus of Nazareth," they replied. "I am he," Jesus said. Judas, the one who was betraying him, was standing there with them.
When Jesus said, "I am he," they stepped back and fell to the ground.
Again he asked them, "Who are you looking for?" They said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered, "I have told you that I am he. If you are looking for me, then let these men go."
This happened so that the words he had spoken would come true: "I have not lost one of those you gave me."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, pulled it out and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus told Peter, "Put your sword away! Shall I not drink the cup of suffering that the Father has given me?"
Then the group of soldiers, with their commander and the Jewish guards, arrested Jesus. They tied him up
and took him first to Annas. Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish leaders that it would be better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and another follower were following Jesus. Because this other follower was known to the high priest, he went with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard.
But Peter had to wait outside at the gate. So the other follower, who was known to the high priest, came back. He spoke to the young woman on duty at the gate and brought Peter in.
The young woman at the gate asked Peter, "You are not one of this man's followers too, are you?" He replied, "No, I am not."
It was cold, so the servants and guards had made a charcoal fire and were standing around it to warm themselves. Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about his followers and his teaching.
Jesus answered, "I have spoken openly for the world to hear. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jewish people come together. I have said nothing in secret.
Why are you questioning me? Ask the people who heard me. They know what I said."
When Jesus said this, one of the guards standing nearby slapped him across the face. "Is that how you answer the high priest?" he demanded.
Jesus replied, "If I said something wrong, tell everyone what was wrong. But if I spoke the truth, why did you hit me?"
Then Annas sent him, still tied up, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Meanwhile, Simon Peter was still standing there warming himself. So they asked him, "You are not one of his followers too, are you?" He denied it, saying, "No, I am not."
One of the high priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Did I not see you with him in the garden?"
Again Peter denied it, and at that moment a rooster began to crow.

Then the Jewish leaders took Jesus from Caiaphas to the palace of the Roman governor. It was early in the morning. They did not go into the palace themselves, because they did not want to become ceremonially unclean. They wanted to be able to eat the Passover meal.
So Pilate came out to them and asked, "What charge are you bringing against this man?"
They answered, "If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you."
Pilate said, "Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law." The Jewish leaders objected, "But we do not have the right to put anyone to death."
This happened so that what Jesus had said about the kind of death he would die would come true.
Then Pilate went back inside the palace. He called Jesus and asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus asked, "Is that your own idea, or did others tell you about me?"
Pilate replied, "Do you think I am a Jew? It was your own people and your chief priests who handed you over to me. What have you done?"
Jesus said, "My kingdom does not belong to this world. If it did, my servants would fight to stop me being handed over to the Jewish leaders. But my kingdom is not from here."

"So you are a king, then!" said Pilate. Jesus answered, "You are right to say that I am a king. In fact, the reason I was born and came into the world is to tell people the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to me."
"What is truth?" Pilate asked. Then he went out again to the Jewish leaders and said, "I find no reason at all to charge him with a crime.
But you have a custom that I set one prisoner free for you at Passover time. Do you want me to set free 'the king of the Jews'?"
They shouted back, "No, not him! Give us Barabbas!" Barabbas was a robber.
